newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Police search mine in Belgian child sex scandal.
newsitem.headline: Police search mine in Belgian child sex scandal.

text.p: Police searched a mine shaft on Monday in their hunt for more clues or bodies in the scandal of child abduction, sexual abuse and murder that has shaken Belgium to the core since news first broke in mid-August.

The main focus of police attention now is an abandoned mine shaft near a property in the Jumet suburb of the southen city of Charleroi linked to convicted rapist Marc Dutroux, a key suspect in the case.
The search, ordered after Dutroux told investigators the shaft might reveal "interesting" information, began late on Friday night and has since continued without break.
The phrase "interesting" is one that Dutroux has used twice before, Belgian media noted on Monday. In both previous cases the bodies of dead children have been found.
To date four dead girls -- two who had starved to death -- have been found in shallow graves on properties linked to Dutroux.
Two other young sexually-abused girls were rescued from a secret dungeon in one of Dutroux's six houses in the area, and police are searching for at least seven other missing children.
Gendarmerie spokesman Jean-Marie Boudin told reporters the searchers had no idea what, if anything, they might find.
But he said they were looking for bodies, guns and other clues to the paedophile gang's activities which are known to have included car theft and drugs trafficking.
So far 13 people have been charged in the affair, including Dutroux's second wife Michelle Martin, Brussels businessman Jean-Michel Nihoul and two senior policemen.
